staged_source_snapshot.description: Stage 01 reproduced the crash against this staged vulnerable checkout.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 64522 (opensc): AddressSanitizer stack-buffer-overflow READ of size 8 in asn1_decode_entry while fuzzing fuzz_pkcs11.
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json issue_description / sanitizer_trace.txt / reproduction_report.json / patch.diff / staged vulnerable source
bug_description.normalized: The exact 775-byte binary witness in `poc` drives the staged `fuzz_pkcs11` binary through synthetic PKCS#15/PIV initialization until `sc_pkcs15_read_certificate()` parses an X.509 certificate and `sc_pkcs15_pubkey_from_spki_fields()` decodes its `subjectPublicKeyInfo`. `sc_asn1_decode_algorithm_id()` parses that `AlgorithmIdentifier`, leaves the remaining parameter bytes in `in,len`, and maps the decoded OID to one of the DES-family table entries whose callback is `asn1_decode_des_params()`; the saved stack proves that callback executed. `asn1_decode_des_params()` then prepares the IV OCTET STRING entry with `sc_format_asn1_entry(asn1_des_iv + 0, iv, &ivlen, 0)`, but `ivlen` is only a 4-byte `int`. The generic ASN.1 decoder later treats every OCTET STRING entry length pointer as `size_t *`, so `c = objlen > *len ? *len : objlen;` performs an 8-byte read from the 4-byte `ivlen` stack slot. AddressSanitizer reports `stack-buffer-overflow READ of size 8` at `src/libopensc/asn1.c:1588`, and its frame report identifies `ivlen` in `asn1_decode_des_params()` as the partially overflowed object. The fix closes this exact contract violation by changing `ivlen` from `int` to `size_t` before passing `&ivlen` into `sc_format_asn1_entry()`.

source.description: First project parser statement on the vulnerable path that consumes the attacker-controlled `AlgorithmIdentifier` bytes and materializes both the decoded OID and the remaining parameter slice.
source.value_from: The exact witness is the 775-byte binary file `gt_results/arvo_64522/poc` (sha256 `bd0e4cf0a02a8be3a1b56f862330d5a2179d932bde397831d3d736dd97945306`). The saved ASan stack shows `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput -> ... -> sc_pkcs15_read_certificate -> parse_x509_cert -> sc_pkcs15_pubkey_from_spki_fields -> sc_asn1_decode_algorithm_id`; by the time this statement runs, `in,len` hold the certificate's attacker-controlled `subjectPublicKeyInfo` `AlgorithmIdentifier` bytes.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

root_cause.description: Root cause. The DES-parameter decoder stores `&ivlen` as the IV OCTET STRING length pointer even though `ivlen` is only a 4-byte `int`, violating the generic ASN.1 decoder's `size_t *` length contract.
root_cause.note: Line 48 declares `int ivlen = 8`, and `c_asn1_des_iv` defines the IV entry as a non-ALLOC OCTET STRING with flags 0. This line therefore records a too-small stack object behind the length pointer that the later non-ALLOC OCTET STRING path will dereference. The patch fixes this exact mismatch by changing `ivlen` to `size_t` before this call.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer crash site. The OCTET STRING decoder dereferences `len` as an 8-byte `size_t *` even though it aliases the 4-byte stack `ivlen` object from `asn1_decode_des_params()`.
sink.note: The saved ASan report says `READ of size 8` at `src/libopensc/asn1.c:1588:18` and identifies local stack object `ivlen` at `src/libopensc/pkcs15-algo.c:48` (`[176,180)`) as the partially overflowed object.

tainted_value_origin.description: This parse step is where the attacker-controlled `AlgorithmIdentifier` becomes the OID plus the remaining parameter slice that step 2 forwards into the vulnerable DES IV decoder.

parser_admitted.code: r = sc_asn1_decode(ctx, asn1_cert, obj, objlen, NULL, NULL);
parser_admitted.description: The saved stack shows the witness already reached X.509 certificate parsing in the synthetic PIV path. On the crashing execution this call accepts the certificate body far enough to invoke `sc_pkcs15_pubkey_from_spki_fields()` for `subjectPublicKeyInfo` instead of rejecting the input earlier.

evidence_limitations: `run_flags.json` sets `runtime_disambiguation` to false, so Stage 02 did not add instrumentation. The chain is grounded only in the staged vulnerable source, `patch.diff`, the saved ASan traces, and `reproduction_report.json`.

The algorithm table shows that both `SC_ALGORITHM_DES` and `SC_ALGORITHM_3DES` dispatch to `asn1_decode_des_params()`. The static artifacts prove that one of those entries matched, but they do not distinguish which exact OID appeared in the witness; that ambiguity does not affect the vulnerable path because both use the same decoder.

The PoC is a full `fuzz_pkcs11` corpus file rather than a standalone extracted certificate. Stage 02 therefore does not claim a precise byte offset for the nested `AlgorithmIdentifier` inside the 775-byte witness beyond the parser path proven by the saved stack and staged source.
Stage 02 did not execute the fixed image, so `sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves` remains false even though `patch.diff` changes the exact width mismatch described above.

fine_trace.note: Source. This call parses the attacker-controlled `AlgorithmIdentifier` sequence from `subjectPublicKeyInfo`. After it returns, `id->oid` is populated and the by-reference `in,len` pair points at any remaining parameter bytes that were not consumed by the OID/optional NULL template.

Using the OID and remainder from step 1, `sc_asn1_get_algorithm_info(id)` selects an algorithm-table entry. The table at `pkcs15-algo.c:375-388` shows both DES and 3DES map to `asn1_decode_des_params`; the saved stack proves this callback executed, which also implies the `if (asn1_alg_id[1].flags & SC_ASN1_PRESENT)` rejection did not fire.

Root cause. `ivlen` is the 4-byte `int` declared at line 48, but this line records `&ivlen` as the IV entry's length pointer. Because the `c_asn1_des_iv` template has flags 0, the later OCTET STRING decoder will use its non-ALLOC path with this pointer. The patch changes `ivlen` to `size_t` before this call.

When the generic decoder processes that IV entry, it unconditionally casts `entry->arg` to `size_t *`. For the state from step 3, `len` now aliases the 4-byte `ivlen` stack slot as though it were an 8-byte length object.

Sink. Evaluating `*len` in the non-ALLOC `SC_ASN1_OCTET_STRING` branch performs an 8-byte read from the stack location that actually holds 4-byte `ivlen`. ASan reports `READ of size 8` at this line and the frame report in `asn1_decode_des_params()` identifies `ivlen` at line 48 as partially overflowed.

allocation_context.note: ASan identifies local stack object `ivlen` at line 48 occupying `[176,180)` in this frame.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: The crash is reported in `asn1_decode_entry()`, but ASan's frame report names stack object `ivlen` in `asn1_decode_des_params()` as the partially overflowed object. The fine trace closes that gap by showing step 3 stores `&ivlen` in the ASN.1 entry and steps 4-5 reinterpret and dereference it as `size_t *`.
cross_validation.patch_resolves_note: The staged patch changes `ivlen` from `int` to `size_t` before passing `&ivlen` to `sc_format_asn1_entry()`, matching the `size_t *` contract later enforced at `asn1_decode_entry()`.

poc.trigger: The staged reproduction command `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_64522 run --version vulnerable --expect crash` reproduces `AddressSanitizer: stack-buffer-overflow READ of size 8 in asn1_decode_entry`.

format.name: fuzz_pkcs11 binary corpus
format.contract: The staged PoC is the exact 775-byte binary witness in `poc` (sha256 `bd0e4cf0a02a8be3a1b56f862330d5a2179d932bde397831d3d736dd97945306`). Its verified trigger semantics are only that this corpus drives `fuzz_pkcs11` through certificate parsing and into a `subjectPublicKeyInfo` `AlgorithmIdentifier` whose decoded OID dispatches to `asn1_decode_des_params()`. That is sufficient because the vulnerability is the wrong-width `ivlen` pointer registered inside that callback, not a finer-grained arithmetic condition on the parameter bytes. The static Stage 02 artifacts do not establish a narrower byte offset for the nested DER field or whether the matched DES-family OID was DES or 3DES.
